arxiv-1906-07124.title: Slicing the IO execution with ReLayTracer
arxiv-1906-07124.creator: Ganguk Lee, Yeaseul Park, Jeongseob Ahn, Youngjin Kwon
arxiv-1906-07124.description: Abstract Analyzing IO performance anomalies is a crucial task in various computing environments, ranging from large-scale cloud applications to desktop applications. However, the IO stack of modern operating systems is complicated, making it hard to understand the performance anomalies with existing tools.

arxiv-1908-08224.title: Analysis of Volterra Integrodifferential Equations with Nonlocal and Boundary Conditions via Picard Operator
arxiv-1908-08224.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by . This article investigates the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the second order Volterra integrodifferential equations with nonlocal and boundary conditions through its integral equivalent equations and fixed point of Banach. Further, utilising the Picard operator theory we obtain the dependency of solutions on the initial nonlocal data and on functions involved on the right hand side of the equations. arxiv-2107-05409.title: Geographic characterization of railway systems
arxiv-2107-05409.creator: Mark M. Dekker
arxiv-2107-05409.description: Abstract Railway systems provide pivotal support to modern societies, making their efficiency and robustness important to ensure. However, these systems are susceptible to disruptions and delays, leading to accumulating economic damage. The large spatial scale of delay spreading typically make it difficult to distinguish which regions will ultimately affected from an initial disruption, creating uncertainty for risk assessment.

arxiv-2309-08419.title: Explicit solutions and linear inviscid damping in the Euler-Boussinesq equation near a stratified Couette flow in the periodic strip
arxiv-2309-08419.creator: Michele Coti Zelati, Marc Nualart
arxiv-2309-08419.description: Abstract . This short note provides explicit solutions to the linearized Boussinesq equations around the stably stratified Couette flow posed on 𝕋 × ℝ {\mathbb{T}}\times{\mathbb{R}} . We consider the long-time behavior of such solutions and prove inviscid damping of the perturbed density and velocity field for any positive Richardson number, with optimal rates.

arxiv-2402-08495.title: A Physics-Informed Deep Learning Description of Knudsen Layer Reactivity Reduction
arxiv-2402-08495.creator: Christopher J. McDevitt, Xian-Zhu Tang
arxiv-2402-08495.description: Abstract A physics-informed neural network (PINN) is used to evaluate the fast ion distribution in the hot spot of an inertial confinement fusion target. The use of tailored input and output layers to the neural network is shown to enable a PINN to learn the parametric solution to the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation in the absence of any synthetic or experimental data.

arxiv-2403-04119.title: Shalika newforms for GL( n n )
arxiv-2403-04119.creator: Takeo Okazaki
arxiv-2403-04119.description: Abstract . Let ( π , V ) (\pi,V) be a generic irreducible representation of a general linear group over a p p -adic field. Jacquet, Piatetski-Shapiro, and Shalika gave an open compact subgroup K K , so that the subspace V K V^{K} consisting of v ∈ V v\in V fixed by K K is one-dimensional.

arxiv-2408-05700.title: Social feedback amplifies emotional language in online video live chats
arxiv-2408-05700.creator: Yishan Luo, Didier Sornette, Sandro Claudio Lera
arxiv-2408-05700.description: Abstract A growing share of human interactions now occurs online, where the expression and perception of emotions are often amplified and distorted. Yet, the interplay between different emotions and the extent to which they are driven by external stimuli or social feedback remains poorly understood.

arxiv-2501-16797.title: Assessing the validity of the anelastic and Boussinesq approximations to model solar inertial modes
arxiv-2501-16797.creator: Suprabha Mukhopadhyay, Yuto Bekki, Xiaojue Zhu, Laurent Gizon
arxiv-2501-16797.description: Abstract Context. Global-scale inertial modes of oscillations have been recently observed on the Sun. They might play an important dynamic and diagnostic role for the Sun. Aims. This work aims to assess the validity of simplifying assumptions in the continuity equation, which have often been used in the linear models of solar inertial modes. Methods.

arxiv-2503-08073.title: Seeing Beyond Haze: Generative Nighttime Image Dehazing
arxiv-2503-08073.creator: Beibei Lin Stephen Lin Robby Tan
arxiv-2503-08073.description: Abstract Nighttime image dehazing is particularly challenging when dense haze and intense glow severely degrade or completely obscure background information. Existing methods often encounter difficulties due to insufficient background priors and limited generative ability, both essential for handling such conditions.

arxiv-2602-16627.title: Dynamic effects of external axion fields in a system of many particles with spin
arxiv-2602-16627.creator: Mariya Iv. Trukhanova 1,2, Yuri N. Obukhov 2,3
arxiv-2602-16627.description: Abstract We develop the theoretical model that describes dynamic non-equilibrium effects of external inertial and axion fields in a system of particles with spin. The possibility of using the spin density and the current density of non-relativistic quantum particle systems for the detection of the hypothetical axion-like dark matter is discussed.

pmc-10651909.title: Polysorbate 80 surface modified SLNs of formoterol suppress SNCA gene and mitochondrial oxidative stress in mice model of Parkinson’s disease
pmc-10651909.creator: Piyong Sola, Kusuma Kumari Garikapati, Praveen Thaggikuppe Krishnamurthy, Mamta Kumari
pmc-10651909.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The present study hypothesises that the selective brain β2 receptor activation through β2-adrenoreceptor agonist (β2ARA), Formoterol (FMT), suppresses SNCA gene expression, a pathological hallmark of Parkinson’s disease (PD) in brain. Further, it is also hypothesized that brain targeted delivery of Formoterol via polysorbate-80 surface modified solid lipid nanoparticles of Formoterol (FMT-SLNs-PS80) can improve its stability, therapeutic efficacy and avoid/reduce peripheral off-target side effects.

pmc-10709543.title: PredictONCO: a web tool supporting decision-making in precision oncology by extending the bioinformatics predictions with advanced computing and machine learning
pmc-10709543.creator: Jan Stourac, Simeon Borko, Rayyan T Khan, Petra Pokorna, Adam Dobias, Joan Planas-Iglesias, Stanislav Mazurenko, Gaspar Pinto, Veronika Szotkowska, Jaroslav Sterba, Ondrej Slaby, Jiri Damborsky, David Bednar
pmc-10709543.description: PredictONCO 1.0 is a unique web server that analyzes effects of mutations on proteins frequently altered in various cancer types. The server can assess the impact of mutations on the protein sequential and structural properties and apply a virtual screening to identify potential inhibitors that could be used as a highly individualized therapeutic approach, possibly based on the drug repurposing.

pmc-11377356.title: A Young Man With Tuberculosis in the Neck Soft Tissue: A Case Report
pmc-11377356.creator: Xiuming Wang, Haomei Luan, Zheyuan Zhang, Huabin Zhang
pmc-11377356.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Tuberculosis (TB) is a preventable and curable disease. TB characteristically causes lung infections, giving rise to pulmonary TB. Many extra-pulmonary organs, including soft tissues, may also be affected, often resulting in non-specific clinical features that make disease diagnosis difficult. We present the case of a 28-year-old male who presented with a soft tissue mass in the left neck accompanied by local redness and tenderness for several months.

pmc-11448049.title: Outcome of flexible fixation for acute isolated syndesmotic injuries
pmc-11448049.creator: Hossam El-Azab, Abdel Rhman Hafez, Mohamed A. Mohamed, Moustafa Elsayed
pmc-11448049.description: BackgroundManagement of syndesmotic injuries with screw fixation has potential disadvantages, which may lead to the loss of some of the ankle functions. The use of the suture-button system instead can overcome these disadvantages.Patients and methodsIn a prospective study, 32 patients with acute isolated syndesmotic injuries were treated with a suture-button device.

pmc-11671995.title: Two-year outcomes of Xen 45 gel stent implantation in patients with open-angle glaucoma: real-world data from the Fight Glaucoma Blindness registry
pmc-11671995.creator: Louis Arnould, Elise Balsat, Yohei Hashimoto, Andrew White, George Kong, Hamish Dunn, Leo Fan, Pierre-Henry Gabrielle, Alain M Bron, Catherine P Creuzot-Garcher, Mitchell Lawlor
pmc-11671995.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveTo evaluate efficacy and safety outcomes of the Xen 45 gel stent implant over 24 months of follow-up.MethodsA retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from the Fight Glaucoma Blindness observational registry. Complete success (CS) was defined as intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction ≥20% from preoperative and an IOP ≤18 mm Hg and ≥6 mm Hg with no secondary procedure at 2 years and without IOP-lowering medications.

pmc-12449672.title: Connectivity of Coral Reefs Along the Kuroshio Current Calls for Transboundary Conservation Strategies
pmc-12449672.creator: Naoki Saito, Akira Iguchi
pmc-12449672.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Environmental conservation becomes more effective when ecological connectivity between patchy habitats is maintained. The coral reef ecosystems of the Yaeyama and Miyako Islands (YAE) in Japan are highly biodiverse and culturally significant but have deteriorated over recent decades. Although coral larvae are expected to be supplied to YAE via the Kuroshio Current from regions outside Japan, previous population genetic and biophysical studies have focused exclusively on connectivity among Japanese coral populations.

pmc-12753483.title: Efficacy and safety of the neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy with pembrolizumab plus docetaxel and cisplatin in resectable locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck
pmc-12753483.creator: Jing Wang, Wenqian Zhang, Dongning Huang, Zhu Liu, Wei Zhang, Zhendong Li
pmc-12753483.description: BackgroundHead and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is the most common type of tumor originating from the squamous epithelium of the oral cavity, oropharynx, larynx and hypopharynx. There is an urgent need to enhance therapeutic efficacy and ensure the function preservation of HNSCC treatment.

pmc-13017717.title: Hypophosphatasia—pathophysiological understanding, preclinical data looking beyond the skeleton, and upcoming treatments
pmc-13017717.creator: Jose Luis Millán
pmc-13017717.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Hypophosphatasia (HPP) is a genetic disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in the ALPL gene that encodes tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (TNAP), an enzyme essential for physiological skeletal/dental mineralization. In HPP, TNAP deficiency leads to the accumulation of extracellular pyrophosphate (PPi), a potent inhibitor of calcification, resulting in skeletal and dental hypomineralization, with disease severity varying from the life-threatening perinatal and infantile forms to the milder later-onset forms that manifest in adulthood or only affect the dentition.

pmc-13366671.title: Judicial evaluation of medical consent for patients with impaired decision-making capacity in Japan: a retrospective observational study of court decisions and ethical implications
pmc-13366671.creator: Masayuki Ohira, Satoru Makita, Takashi Osada, Masaki Takao
pmc-13366671.description: BackgroundAdvance care planning and respect for patient autonomy are central concerns in contemporary medical ethics, particularly for patients whose decision-making capacity may be impaired. This study aimed to examine and identify ethical challenges in judicial judgments in Japan relating to these patients.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective observational study of Japanese civil court judgments using Westlaw Japan.

pmc-13368923.title: LTF promotes central nervous system leukemia progression via neutrophil serine proteases
pmc-13368923.creator: Yiran Zhang, Huasong Yu, Zhongxiang Jiao, Ming Yang, Wenshan Zhang, Chaoqun Wang, Hexiao Zhang, Wei Wang, Minghe Zhang, Xiaoyue Li, Lin Song, Bo Jiang, Junyuan Qi, Yinghui Li, Yingdai Gao
pmc-13368923.description: IntroductionCentral nervous system (CNS) infiltration is a severe complication of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), often leading to relapse and poor prognosis. The underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood, limiting the development of effective targeted therapies. Conventional chemotherapy agents capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) carry significant toxicity and fail to eliminate leukemia stem cells.

pmc-13583650.title: Testicular Schistosomiasis Mimicking Testicular Tumour: A Case Report
pmc-13583650.creator: Auwal Idris Kabuga, Rufai Yunusa, Ahmad Hamza, Nura Yusuf, Musbahu Yusuf, Muhammad Yaseen Hassan
pmc-13583650.description: Schistosomiasis is a neglected tropical disease, with the highest burden in Sub-Saharan Africa, predominantly due to Schistosoma haematobium. Testicular involvement is rare; fewer than 30 cases have been reported in the literature to date, though sporadic reports continue to emerge from endemic areas.

pmc-13658336.title: Impact of SGLT2 inhibitors on urinary tract infections in patients with diabetes mellitus and ileal urinary diversion: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13658336.creator: Nicolas Arnold, Ruby Hischier, Mihai Dorin Vartolomei, Laila Schneidewind, Nicola Giudici, Raphael Röthlisberger, Bernhard Kiss, Beat Roth
pmc-13658336.description: PurposeThe impact of sodium–glucose linked transporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) on urinary tract infection (UTI) risk remains uncertain and may be dose-dependent. No prior studies have evaluated their effect in patients with urinary diversion after cystectomy. This study evaluated the association between SGLT2i use and UTI in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) after cystectomy and ileal urinary diversion.
